captions.detailed: A three-branch inspection fixture head consisting of a dark grey rectangular center spine and three light grey articulating arms. The lower arm projects to the side and terminates in a square mounting pad, revolving about a transverse axis. The forward-facing arm projects straight out and terminates in a circular flange with mounting holes, revolving about a vertical stub axis. The upper arm projects to the opposite side, stepping upward to end in a small U-shaped bracket, revolving about a longitudinal axis.
captions.instruction: Generate a three-branch inspection fixture head with a central rectangular spine. The fixture should include a lower side arm revolving about a transverse axis, a forward-facing arm revolving about a vertical stub axis ending in a circular flange, and an upper side arm revolving about a longitudinal axis ending in a U-shaped bracket. Use dark grey for the main spine and collars, and light grey for the articulating arms and mounting pads.
captions.factory: Construct the central rectangular spine using box primitives. Create three distinct collars or housing blocks attached to the spine at different heights and orientations. For each arm branch, model the mounting adapters, cylindrical shafts, and final end-effectors (a square plate, a circular flange with holes, and a U-shaped bracket) using combinations of cylinders, boxes, and boolean operations. Define revolute joints linking each collar housing to its respective arm branch, specifying the correct rotation axes (transverse, vertical, and longitudinal).
